hero.title: Smart contract security: think like an attacker, report like an auditor
hero.subtitle: Break and fix real vulnerable contracts, model attacks with numbers, learn the tools and write the audit findings that clients can act on. Every task is checked and explained.
hero.outcomeLine: After this course you can review a small contract for common vulnerabilities and report your findings clearly.

assessment: Finish the required labs in each module: they are checked automatically and explained when something is missing.
Pass each module quiz (70% or more). Short tests inside the lessons give instant feedback.
Complete the security review and the final assessment.

faq.q: Does the platform run exploits or tests?
faq.a: No. The labs check your analysis, calculations and writing. You run the code yourself in your own tools, on test networks only.

faq.q: Will this make me a qualified auditor?
faq.a: No. It teaches the concepts and the process. Becoming an auditor takes much more practice on real code and mentoring.

faq.q: Is it safe to try attacks?
faq.a: Only on your own contracts on local or test networks. Never attack contracts you do not own or have permission to test.

activities.title: How fast could a reentrancy drain a vault?
activities.objective: Model a reentrancy attack to see why it is so serious. (A teaching model.)
activities.scenario: A vulnerable vault holds other people's money. The attacker deposits a small amount and recursion lets them withdraw it many times per transaction, limited by gas.
steps: In B7 work out what is withdrawn per transaction: the smaller of attacker deposit times recursion depth, and all funds in the vault (including the attacker's deposit).
In B8 work out how many transactions drain the vault: total funds divided by B7, rounded up.
In B9 work out the fees paid: transactions times the fee per transaction.
In B10 work out the attacker's profit: the funds of other people (B2) minus the fees.
In B11 show Exploit pays if the profit is above zero, else Exploit fails.

checks.label: B7 is the withdrawal per transaction
checks.hint: =MIN(B3*B4,B2+B3)
checks.explain: The smaller of the two amounts.

checks.label: B8 is the transactions needed
checks.hint: =ROUNDUP((B2+B3)/B7,0)
checks.explain: Round up: a partial transaction is still a transaction.

checks.label: B11 is the verdict
checks.hint: =IF(B10>0,"Exploit pays","Exploit fails")

activities.title: Measure a rounding loss
activities.objective: Show how integer division can cheat a small depositor.
activities.scenario: A vault holds 1,000,000 units of assets against 1,000 shares. A user deposits 1,500 units. The contract gives INT(deposit × shares ÷ assets) shares.
steps: In B7 work out the shares minted, rounded down with INT.
In B8 work out the value of those shares: shares times assets divided by total shares.
In B9 work out the loss: the deposit minus B8.
In B10 work out the loss as a fraction of the deposit.
In B11 show Rounding loss if B9 is above zero, else No loss.

checks.label: B7 is the shares minted
checks.hint: =INT(B4*B3/B2)
checks.explain: Multiply first, then divide and round down.

checks.label: B11 is the verdict
checks.hint: =IF(B9>0,"Rounding loss","No loss")
checks.explain: A positive loss is a loss.

activities.title: Would a flash-loan attack pay?
activities.objective: Work out whether a price-manipulation attack is profitable after fees.
activities.scenario: An attacker flash-borrows funds, distorts a pool price and gains from a lender that trusts it. (A teaching model, made-up figures.)
steps: In B7 work out the flash loan fee: the amount borrowed times the fee rate.
In B8 work out the gain after the fee: the gross gain minus the flash loan fee.
In B9 work out the profit after the transaction cost: B8 minus the gas cost.
In B10 show Profitable attack if B9 is above zero, else Not profitable.
In B11 work out the profit as a percentage of the gross gain.

checks.label: B8 is the gain after fee
B10 is the verdict
checks.hint: =IF(B9>0,"Profitable attack","Not profitable")

activities.title: Score and rank findings
activities.objective: Rank findings by impact times likelihood and count how many are serious.
activities.scenario: An audit found four issues. Score each from 1 (low) to 3 (high) for impact and likelihood, then label them.
steps: In D2 work out the score: impact times likelihood. Fill down to D5.
In E2 show High if the score is 6 or more, Medium if it is 3 or more, otherwise Low. Fill down to E5.
In B7 count how many findings are High.
In B8 work out the average score.
In B9 find the highest score.

checks.label: E2 is the severity
checks.hint: =IF(D2>=6,"High",IF(D2>=3,"Medium","Low"))

checks.label: E3 is the severity
checks.hint: =IF(D3>=6,"High",IF(D3>=3,"Medium","Low"))

checks.label: E4 is the severity
checks.hint: =IF(D4>=6,"High",IF(D4>=3,"Medium","Low"))

checks.label: B7 counts the High findings
checks.hint: =COUNTIF(E2:E5,"High")

checks.label: B8 is the average score
checks.hint: =AVERAGE(D2:D5)

checks.label: B9 is the highest score
checks.hint: =MAX(D2:D5)
